ai.description: Trachischium laeve reaches 30–40 cm. It is uniform olive-brown above with a yellowish belly. Key features include smooth, glossy scales and a rounded snout adapted for fossorial life.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trachischium laeve* is best distinguished by its single internasal scale, whereas most similar *Trachischium* species possess a pair of divided internasals.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium laeve* inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and grassy clearings in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Trachischium laeve* is a secretive, fossorial snake that spends most of its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium laeve* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium laeve* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
